svg.title: Figure 4-5. The safety envelope's states (WP-S-03 §4.5)
svg.desc: Safety modes SILENT, NOOUTPUT, ELM327, TOYOTA, OTHER_CAR; authority NOT_ALLOWED, ENGAGE_PENDING, ALLOWED. Revocations: T2 cruise off or cancelled (in the code); T3 brake pressed (in the code); T4 bad checksum, counter or length (in the code, partly met or not assessed); T5 an RX message late or missing (in the code, partly met or not assessed); T6 engaged mismatch, 1 Hz tick (2–3 s) (in the code, partly met or not assessed); T6a engaged mismatch (0.3 s) (in the code); T7 safety mode set again (in the code); T9 frame out of limits (today: dropped) (not in the code); T10a no SoC heartbeat (0.3 s) (in the code, partly met or not assessed); T10b commands stop arriving (50 / 100 ms) (in the code); T10c cruise on with main off (150 ms) (in the code, partly met or not assessed); T10d MCU platform fault (not in the code); T10e driver steers against it (not in the code); T11 TX rate exceeded (in the code); T12 driver torque above the limit (not in the code); T13 SPI errors (not in the code); T14 car CAN bus-off (not in the code); T15 camera-side forwarding lost (not in the code). Host states: Disabled: no authority (agree); Disabled, driver locked out: no authority (agree); Pre-enabled: authority, once granted (agree); Enabled: authority (agree); Overriding: accelerator: authority, longitudinal blocked (agree); Overriding: steering: authority (disagree); Soft disabling: authority for up to 3 s (disagree); Just disabled (immediate): authority ≤ 0.3 s, then none (briefly differ).
svg.text: The panda's safety modes and, in the car mode, its authority to actuate; what takes authority away; and what each driving state of the host means on the car
nothing sent to the car; the MCU's safe
receive only, nothing sent to the car
OTHER_CAR: unreachable in the reference build (M4)
TOYOTA · 73: the car mode, with authority · sm-toy-auth
the 1 s window after a cruise edge
revoke: 11 transitions in the code, 7 not yet (below)
T1a: cruise 0→1 with every RX check valid · T1b: the host's engaged heartbeat within 1 s · T1c: 1 s without it, cruise off, brake.
Upstream build: T1 grants on the cruise edge, with no window.
in the code, partly met or not assessed (5)
an RX message late or missing
cruise on with main off (150 ms) · ref.
Kept, not revoked: EPS reports a fault: lateral frames with torque or steer request refused · gas pressed: longitudinal actuation blocked.
ref. = reference build only. Status from the WP-W-02 Baseline of the software safety requirements each transition cites; nothing is verified on hardware, so it is blue, not green.
Host state → authority on the car
A cruise edge opens the 1 s window; with no engaged heartbeat it closes again (T1c).
NO_ENTRY refuses (N1), so the engaged heartbeat never comes and the window closes
(T1c). Upstream build: granted on the edge (T1) until the cruise drops or T6 revokes.
The engaged heartbeat grants in the window (T1b); a brake pressed while moving closes
Granted by the engaged heartbeat inside the window (T1b).
Gas blocks longitudinal frames; authority is kept.
⚠ The envelope does not see it: T10e and T12 are not in the code.
⚠ The host winds down while the envelope still grants (GAP-16).
The engaged heartbeat drops; T6a revokes within 0.3 s (upstream build: T6, 2–3 s).
Green arrows grant; red revokes; dashed mode arrows step down.

Generated by fig_s03_envelope_states.py from the state-machine records of WP-W-05 §5 (sm-safety-mode, sm-toy-auth, sm-selfdrived); the tables there stay normative and give the code reference of every transition.

g.text: Terms: ALLOWED the envelope's authority state with controls_allowed = 1 (NOT_ALLOWED: 0), WP-W-05 §5.2 · CAN controller area network: the vehicle's data bus · EPS electric power steering · GAP-nn gap found by the gap assessment · M01–M14, M1–M8

guide word M01…M14 of the HARA (no function, unrequested, excessive, …); M1…M8 (one digit) a safety-mode transition (WP-W-05 §5.1) · MCU microcontroller: the panda safety processor (STM32H7) · NOOUTPUT the panda's safety mode that receives but

sends nothing · QM quality managed: no ASIL; ordinary quality processes suffice · RX receive · SILENT the panda's safety mode that sends nothing · SoC system on chip: the comma device's main processor, running openpilot (QM) · SPI serial

peripheral interface (the link between SoC and MCU) · TOYOTA the panda's Toyota car mode (parameter 73 in the reference build) · TSR-nn technical safety requirement (WP-S-02) · TX transmit · WP-nn work product, e.g. WP-C-04; the letter is its
area (M management, C concept, S system, H hardware, W software, V validation, P processes, A analyses, O operation, K safety case)
